description: Look of the shaft internal-load arrows of the native export (--shaft-loads, #15150 Track Z, Z9c).

bending.legend: Shaft bending, {part} [N m]: proximal-on-tip-side moment at each shaft joint, right-hand rule; 1 m = {per_m:g} N m

shear.legend: Shaft shear, {part} [N]: proximal-on-tip-side force normal to the shaft at each joint; 1 m = {per_m:g} N

sources.bending.scale_m: Arrow metres per N m. Bending at a chain joint is its spring moment (stiffness times bend); on the synthetic seed driver chain a 0.02 rad bend gives 3 to 7.6 N m tip to grip, drawn 7.5 to 19 cm, legible at preview size; 16 N m reaches max_length_m.
sources.shear.scale_m: Arrow metres per N. On the synthetic seed driver chain the shear is 3 to 11 N through the downswing, drawn 1.5 to 5.5 cm; 80 N reaches max_length_m.
sources.parts.hex: Cyan, lime and violet: outside the force-kind palette (palette.py), the hand tip-to-tail blue/vermillion/white, the lead/trail blue/yellow and the tension blue/compression red, so a shaft arrow is never read as a joint torque or a grip force.
sources.sign_convention: Frame of shaft_load_split.py: the wrench the proximal side (toward the grip) applies to the distal, tip-ward chain, world frame; bending is its moment normal to the shaft axis, shear its force normal to the axis.
